scams.location: Vieux Lyon, Place Bellecour, Part-Dieu station, Perrache station, Confluence Tram stop, Metro Line D, T2 tram line, Basilica of Notre-Dame de Fourvière
scams.story: Pickpockets in Lyon operate in tourist-heavy areas and on crowded public transport. They often work in teams using distraction techniques - one person might ask for directions, bump into you, or create a commotion while an accomplice steals your wallet or phone. At the Confluence Tram stop, groups of women wearing large bags have been observed surrounding tourists to access backpacks. On metro Line D and the T2 tram, pickpockets are most active during rush hour boarding and exiting when movement is chaotic.
red_flags: Being surrounded by strangers asking questions
Someone bumping into you repeatedly
Groups of people getting unusually close
Chaotic boarding situations on public transport
how_to_avoid: Wear bags across your body with zippers facing inward
Keep only minimal cash and one card on you
Use money belts or hidden pouches
Stay alert during metro boarding and exiting

scams.story: Ticket touts approach tourists who appear lost or confused at major Lyon train stations. They offer to sell metro tickets at seemingly reasonable prices, but the tickets are either fake, expired, or already used. The scammer may claim they have 'extra' tickets or offer a 'discount' compared to the official ticket machines. When you try to use the ticket, it won't work at the turnstile.
red_flags: Strangers approaching you near ticket machines
Offers of discounted tickets
Sellers not in official TCL uniforms
how_to_avoid: Only buy tickets from official TCL machines or counters
Use the TCL mobile app for digital tickets
Ignore anyone offering to sell tickets outside official channels

scams.location: Rue de la République, Part-Dieu station, Perrache station, Place Bellecour
scams.story: Someone approaches with a clipboard asking 'Do you speak English?' and requests you sign a petition for a charity supporting deaf-mute individuals. After signing, they flip the clipboard to reveal a donation section and pressure you to give money. While you're distracted with the clipboard, an accomplice may pickpocket you from behind.
red_flags: Petition only in English in a French-speaking city
Immediate request for cash donation after signing
Others hovering nearby while you interact
how_to_avoid: Simply say 'Non, merci' and keep walking
Never sign anything handed to you on the street
Legitimate charities in France only ask for email addresses, not cash

scams.location: Vieux Lyon (Old Town), Presqu'île, Rue Mercière
scams.story: Tourist-centric restaurants near Lyon's historic areas may present inflated bills. Tactics include: adding items you didn't order, charging for bread and water that appeared 'free,' using 'tourist menus' with elevated prices. Some establishments trade on Lyon's reputation as France's gastronomic capital to justify excessive prices for mediocre food.
red_flags: No prices listed on menus outside
Menus only in French with no translations
Aggressive touts outside trying to pull you in
how_to_avoid: Check prices before sitting down
Ask for itemized bills and review carefully
Eat where locals eat, away from main tourist streets

scams.location: Busy tourist areas, Near major attractions, Metro exits
scams.story: A scammer sets up a makeshift table with three cups or cards. They invite you to bet on guessing the ball's location. 'Winners' in the crowd are accomplices who pretend to win to draw you in. The game is completely rigged through sleight of hand - you cannot win.
red_flags: Crowd of 'players' who seem unusually lucky
High-pressure atmosphere encouraging large bets
Game operators who can pack up in seconds
how_to_avoid: Never play street gambling games - they are always rigged
Do not stop to watch
Remember that bystanders are likely accomplices

scams.location: Tourist walkways, Near bridges, Pedestrian areas
scams.story: A person 'finds' a gold ring on the ground near you and asks if you dropped it. When you say no, they show you a marking claiming it's real gold and offer to sell it for a 'good price.' The ring is worthless brass. They may also ask for money 'for food' or 'for their children.'
red_flags: Someone 'finding' something valuable right next to you
Claims of precious metal markings
Emotional appeals about needing money for family
how_to_avoid: Don't engage - say 'Non' and keep walking
Never accept items 'found' on the street

scams.location: Tourist attractions, Near churches, Pedestrian areas
scams.story: A vendor approaches and grabs your hand, quickly weaving a colorful friendship bracelet around your wrist. Once tied on with a difficult knot, they demand payment of 10-20 euros. If you refuse, they become aggressive or an accomplice uses the distraction to pickpocket you.
red_flags: Anyone reaching for your hand unexpectedly
Offers of 'free' gifts or demonstrations
String or craft materials visible
how_to_avoid: Keep your hands in your pockets when approached
Say 'Non' firmly and keep walking
Don't let anyone touch you or attach anything

scams.location: Restaurant terraces, Romantic spots, Evening entertainment areas
scams.story: A seller approaches couples dining outdoors, offering a rose with 'Flower for the pretty lady!' The moment you touch or accept the flower, they demand 5-10 euros. If you try to return it, they refuse and become aggressive until you pay out of embarrassment.
red_flags: Anyone approaching your table with flowers
Flowers being pushed into your hands
how_to_avoid: Don't touch or accept any flowers offered
A simple 'Non, merci' and wave sends them away
Ask restaurant staff to intervene if needed

scams.location: Metro stations, Tourist areas, Near bars at night
scams.story: Criminals pose as police officers, quickly flashing fake badges. They claim they need to check your wallet for counterfeit bills or 'drug money.' While examining your wallet, they steal cash. Sometimes a 'tourist' accomplice first asks you to break a large bill, then the fake officer arrives.
red_flags: Anyone stopping you to exchange money just before 'police' arrive
Officers in plain clothes rather than uniform
Quick badge flashes without allowing inspection
how_to_avoid: Know that real police never ask to see your wallet - only ID documents
Suggest going to the nearest police station to verify their identity
Call 17 if unsure

scams.location: Lyon-Saint Exupéry Airport, Part-Dieu station, Perrache station, Outside nightclubs
scams.story: Unscrupulous taxi drivers target tourists unfamiliar with Lyon's layout. They may take long routes to inflate the fare, 'forget' to start the meter, or select the higher night/weekend rate during regular hours. Airport runs are particularly vulnerable - the fare from Lyon-Saint Exupéry to the city center should be around €50-70.
red_flags: Driver not starting the meter
Meter showing night rate during daytime
Driver taking unfamiliar routes
how_to_avoid: Only use taxis from official ranks
Ensure the meter is zeroed before departure
Use GPS on your phone to follow the route
Consider using Uber or Bolt

scams.location: Private ATMs in tourist areas, ATMs on busy streets, Near train stations
scams.story: Criminals attach skimming devices to ATMs that steal your card data and PIN. Private ATM companies like Euronet place machines that charge excessive fees and poor exchange rates - up to 4x more than bank ATMs. They may offer Dynamic Currency Conversion at terrible rates.
red_flags: ATMs that look modified or have loose parts
ATMs branded with non-bank names (Euronet, Travelex)
Prompts offering to convert to your home currency
how_to_avoid: Use ATMs inside bank branches only
Look for major French banks: BNP Paribas, Société Générale, LCL
Always cover keypad when entering PIN
Decline dynamic currency conversion

scams.story: Someone asks you to take their photo using their camera. After you return the camera, they claim you broke it and demand money for repairs. The 'camera' was already broken - they use it repeatedly for this scam.
red_flags: Insistence on using their camera rather than phone
Old or unusual looking camera equipment
Aggressive reaction that seems disproportionate
how_to_avoid: Politely decline to take photos with others' cameras
If accused of damage, suggest filing a police report together - scammers will refuse

research_notes: Research for France Travel Scams book. Lyon.
